visual.title: The three Reasoning Beyond tasks
visual.alt: Three columns. Apply: stems ask which scenario the author would consider an example of a passage concept; the move is to abstract the principle into one general sentence and then match structure; traps are a superficial match sharing vocabulary but not logic, the opposite case, and a principle the passage never endorsed. Strengthen or weaken: stems ask which finding, if true, would most affect the argument; the move is to name the central assumption first and ask whether the choice validates or attacks it; traps are irrelevant information, the wrong direction, proving too much, and a scope mismatch. Extend: stems ask what the author would most likely agree with; the move is to ask what else must be true if the argument is sound, requiring entailment rather than consistency; traps are the too-extreme extension, the merely consistent answer, and guessing from the author's personality. A footer advises predicting before reading the choices, matching on logical structure rather than topic, and remembering that a strengthener need only make the conclusion likelier.
visual.caption: Track the author's logic — not whether the author is right.
